correctness.rationale: For the exactly specified parent density f_T(t;a)=a^2(a+t)e^(-at)/(a^2+1), independent of the unit transform X=T/(1+T), differentiate log f twice. Expected minus second derivative equals 2(3a^2+1)/(a^2(a^2+1)^2)+a^2/(a^2+1)e^(a^2)E1(a^2). The last term follows from integral of e^(-at)/(a+t). E1 asymptotics give lim(a sqrt I)=sqrt 2 as a->0 and =1 at infinity, proving Jeffreys sqrt I cannot be proportional to 1/a. For sample t_i=x_i/(1-x_i)>0, the log-uniform posterior is O(a^(2n-1)) near 0 and O(a^(n-1)e^(-a sum t_i)) at infinity, hence proper for all interior nonempty samples. Independent mpmath quadrature at a=.03,.2,1,4,30 agrees with the expectation and limiting behavior.
